G01.notes: Three goals connect environment-dependent feeding, inherited population change and limited inference with observed comparisons, percentage/change decisions, checks and original explanations; no mastery inferred from completion.

G02.notes: Four distinct seed/beak pairings and one generation in each matched habitat; independent populations/repeats are distinguished from individual birds and alternative model branches.

G03.notes: Michigan and OpenStax institutional teaching sources read. Existing variation, differing survival and inherited contribution are consistent across model/art/text. Exact numerical rules are synthetic, not real finch data; no need-driven adult change or speciation claim.

G04.notes: Time units, fixed rates, rounded population size, example family, continuous/polygenic real traits, no stochastic drift and other omissions are explained near results and in reports/resources.

G05.notes: Actual seed-to-beak and surviving-pair-to-nest placement changes seed evidence/family view. Students interpret new-generation proportions and compare environments; model-provided remainder is labeled.

G06.notes: Initial/intermediate/final feeding and both habitat states inspected on desktop and phone/tablet. Shaded birds, beaks, seeds, shell fragments, nest and supporting perch are plausible illustrations. Shared geometry keeps sites aligned and tools clear.

G07.notes: Choice shuffle is stable per seeded attempt/reload. Beak/seed/habitat identities and numerical relationships are preserved; choices do not identify correctness by fixed position.
